column2: Write a product description for [product name]. It's a [type of product] for [who it's for]. Key features: [list 3-5 features]. What makes it different: [your unique selling points]. Price: [price]. Write: (1) A short version (50 words) for product cards/listings, (2) A medium version (150 words) for the product page, (3) A long version (300 words) for a sales page or email that tells the story of why this product exists and why it's worth it. Focus on benefits over features. Use sensory, specific language — not vague marketing speak.

Write a weekly team update email for my team of [number of people]. We're a [describe company — type, industry, stage].
This week's contents:
- Key wins: [list raw bullet points]
- Challenges/blockers: [describe]
- Client updates: [any notable client news]
- New hires/departures: [if any]
- Process changes: [anything changing]
- Upcoming deadlines: [list]
- Fun stuff: [birthdays, milestones, team events, or just a good meme/quote]
Structure it to be scannable (no one reads a wall of text from their boss). Include section headers, bold key names and deadlines, and keep the whole thing under 400 words. Tone: [leadership style — e.g., "transparent, slightly casual, motivating"]. End with an ask or a question that invites replies.
